prediction.rationale: Tests whether the methodology recognizes extreme substrate-stress in Texas Q2-2000 → Q2-2001 wholesale electricity market. Recognition criterion: ratio of peak-monthly-mean spot price in event window to median spot price in baseline window > 10x. Does NOT pre-assert that this means 'substrate failed to commodify' — that is downstream synthesis per §4.2 reframe. The voice reports criterion-fires + observed value only.

kill_condition.rule: fail if peak-event-window-monthly-spot / baseline-median-monthly-spot < 10.0 (recognition criterion does not fire — substrate did not exhibit extreme spot-price instability at the pre-committed threshold)
kill_condition.rationale: Single composite metric: peak-monthly-mean-spot in event window divided by median-monthly-spot in baseline window. Threshold 10x is well below documented ERCOT + FERC/NERC Nov 2021 Report peak figures (~$750-1000/MWh vs ~$25/MWh baseline = ~70x); 10x gives substantial headroom for alternative public-source calibrations.

public_signal_source.feed_name: Texas ISO / PX wholesale spot prices (settlement data)
public_signal_source.citation_anchor: ERCOT post-event report; FERC/NERC Inquiry into Bulk-Power System Events of Feb 2021, March 2003; Texas ISO public settlement archives

verdict.rationale: Recognition criterion FIRES. extreme_spot_price_instability_index = 66.79x (peak 2021-02 $1740.0/MWh vs 2020-12/2021-01 baseline median $26.0/MWh), ≥ 10.0x threshold. Voice reports criterion-fires + observed value; downstream synthesis (whether this constitutes 'substrate failed to commodify' or 'transient extreme event' or 'regulatory-design failure') is left to the Phase-2 interpretation document per §4.2 reframe. v2-ratchet to real ERCOT hourly settlement-point data required for any external claim.
